title.zh: 卷369 列傳一百五十六 林则徐 邓廷桢 达洪阿
title.en: Volume 369 Biographies 156: Lin Zexu, Deng Tingzhen, Da Hong A
title.raw: 卷369 列傳一百五十六 林则徐 邓廷桢 达洪阿

sentences.zh: 林則徐 ，字少穆，福建侯官人。

translations.literal: Lin Zexu, style name Shaomu, was a native of Houguan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu, whose style name was Shaomu, came from Houguan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 少警敏，有異才。

translations.literal: In youth he was alert and keen, and possessed unusual talent.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was quick-witted and showed exceptional ability.

sentences.zh: 年二十，舉鄉試。

translations.literal: At age twenty he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he passed the provincial civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張師誠闢佐幕。

translations.literal: The provincial governor Zhang Shicheng summoned him to serve on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Governor Zhang Shicheng recruited him as a staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1811 he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 歷典江西、雲南鄉試，分校會試。

translations.literal: He successively supervised the provincial examinations in Jiangxi and Yunnan and served as a grader in the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as chief examiner for the provincial examinations in Jiangxi and Yunnan and as a grader for the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 遷御史，疏論福建閩安副將張寶以海盜投誠，宜示裁抑，以防驕蹇，被嘉納。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor and in a memorial argued that Zhang Bao, vice commander at Min'an in Fujian, who had surrendered as a pirate, should be shown restraint and restraint to guard against arrogance and insolence; this was praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to censor, he memorialized that Vice Commander Zhang Bao of Min'an in Fujian, a former pirate who had surrendered, ought to be kept in check lest he grow arrogant and unruly; the court approved his advice.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出為杭嘉湖道，修海塘，興水利。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as intendant of the Hang-Jia-Hu Circuit, repaired sea dikes, and promoted water conservancy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was posted as intendant of the Hangzhou-Jiaxing-Huzhou circuit, where he repaired sea dikes and advanced hydraulic works.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，聞父病，引疾歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang, hearing that his father was ill, he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821, on hearing that his father was ill, he took leave on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 二年，起授淮海道，未之任，署浙江鹽運使。

translations.literal: In the second year he was recalled and appointed intendant of the Huai-Hai Circuit but did not take up the post, and served instead as acting salt transport commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1822 he was recalled and named intendant of the Huai-Hai circuit but never assumed the post, serving instead as acting Zhejiang salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遷江蘇按察使，治獄嚴明。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Jiangsu provincial judicial commissioner and administered cases with strict clarity.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Jiangsu provincial judicial commissioner and gained a reputation for handling cases with rigorous fairness.

sentences.zh: 四年，大水，署布政使，治賑。

translations.literal: In the fourth year there was a great flood; he served as acting provincial treasurer and directed relief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1824, after severe flooding, he acted as provincial treasurer and oversaw disaster relief.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母憂，命赴南河修高家堰堤工，事竣回籍。

translations.literal: Soon after he entered mourning for his mother, he was ordered to go to the Southern Rivers to repair the Gaojia Embankment; when the work was finished he returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, while mourning his mother, he was ordered to the Southern Rivers to repair the Gaojia Embankment; when the project was complete he returned home.

sentences.zh: 六年，命署兩淮鹽政，以未終制辭，服闋，補陝西按察使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered to act as salt commissioner of the Liang-Huai region; he declined because mourning was not yet completed; after mourning ended he was appointed Shaanxi provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1826 he was ordered to act as Liang-Huai salt commissioner but declined while still in mourning; after his mourning period he was appointed Shaanxi provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遷江寧布政使，父憂歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Jiangning provincial treasurer and returned home on mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jiangning provincial treasurer, then went home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 十年，補湖北布政使，調河南，又調江寧。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Hubei provincial treasurer, transferred to Henan, then again to Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In 1830 he was appointed Hubei provincial treasurer, transferred to Henan, then transferred again to Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢河東河道總督。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to director-general of the Eastern Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1831 he was promoted to director-general of the Eastern Rivers.

sentences.zh: 疏陳稭料為河工第一弊藪，親赴各廳察驗；

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated that straw materials were the foremost abuse in river works and personally went to each office to inspect and verify;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that straw materials were the greatest abuse in river works and personally inspected each office;

sentences.zh: 又言碎石實足為埽工之輔，應隨宜施用。

translations.literal: He also said that broken stone was truly sufficient to assist revetment works and should be applied as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that crushed stone could effectively supplement revetment works and should be used wherever appropriate.

sentences.zh: 十二年，調江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to be Jiangsu governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1832 he was transferred to governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 吳中洊飢，奏免逋賦，籌撫卹。

translations.literal: In Wu there was repeated famine; he memorialized to remit arrears in taxes and organized relief.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck the Suzhou region repeatedly; he memorialized for tax remissions and organized relief.

sentences.zh: 前在籓司任，議定賑務章程，行之有效，至是仍其法，宿弊一清。

translations.literal: Previously while serving as provincial treasurer he had drawn up regulations for relief work that proved effective; now he followed the same methods and long-standing abuses were entirely cleared.
translations.idiomatic: While provincial treasurer he had drafted relief regulations that worked well; he now applied the same methods again and cleared away entrenched abuses.

sentences.zh: 賑竣，乃籌積穀備荒。

translations.literal: When relief was finished he then planned to accumulate grain against famine.
translations.idiomatic: After relief was complete he began stockpiling grain against future famine.

sentences.zh: 清釐交代，盡結京控諸獄。

translations.literal: He cleared up handovers of office and settled all cases appealed to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared up official handovers and disposed of all cases pending appeal in the capital.

sentences.zh: 考覈屬吏，疏言：「察吏莫先於自察，必將各屬大小政務，逐一求盡於心，然後能以驗群吏之盡心與否。

translations.literal: Examining subordinate officials, he stated in a memorial: "In inspecting officials nothing comes before self-inspection; one must take every large and small affair of each subordinate jurisdiction and seek to understand it fully in one's own mind, and only then can one verify whether the mass of officials are doing their utmost or not.
translations.idiomatic: In reviewing subordinates he memorialized: "The first step in inspecting officials is to inspect oneself; only when every affair, large or small, in each jurisdiction is fully understood can one judge whether officials are doing their duty.

sentences.zh: 如大吏之心先未貫徹，何從察其情偽？

translations.literal: If the mind of the superior official is not first thoroughly penetrated, how can one investigate truth and falsehood?
translations.idiomatic: If a senior official has not first mastered the facts himself, how can he discern who is sincere and who is not?

sentences.zh: 臣惟持此不敢不盡之心，事事與僚屬求實際。

translations.literal: Your subject holds to this mind that dares not be less than full and in every matter seeks practical results together with colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: I hold myself to this standard of thoroughness and demand practical results from my staff in every matter.

sentences.zh: 」詔嘉之，勉以力行。

translations.literal: " The edict praised him and exhorted him to act with vigor.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor praised him and urged him to persevere.

sentences.zh: 先是總督陶澍奏濬三江，則徐方為臬司，綜理其事，旋以憂去。

translations.literal: Earlier Governor-General Tao Zhu had memorialized to dredge the Three Rivers; Zexu was then provincial judicial commissioner and managed the affair in general, but soon left on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Governor-General Tao Zhu had proposed dredging the Three Rivers; Lin was then judicial commissioner and oversaw the project, but soon left office to mourn.

sentences.zh: 至是黃浦、吳淞工已竣，則徐力任未竟者，劉河工最要，撥帑十六萬五千有奇，白茆次要，官紳集捐十一萬兩，同時開濬，以工代賑。

translations.literal: By then the Huangpu and Wusong works were finished; Zexu took on the unfinished tasks with full effort. The Liu River project was most important: 165,000-odd taels from the treasury were allocated; the Baomao project was secondary: officials and gentry raised 110,000 taels in donations; both were dredged at once, using labor in place of relief.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangpu and Wusong projects were by then complete; Lin took up what remained. The Liu River was the priority, funded with more than 165,000 taels from the treasury; the Baomao channel was secondary, with 110,000 taels raised by officials and gentry; both were dredged at once, labor substituting for relief.

sentences.zh: 兩河舊皆通海，易淤，且鑿河工鉅，改為清水長河，與黃埔、吳淞交匯通流。

translations.literal: Both rivers had formerly connected to the sea, silted easily, and dredging was costly; they were changed into long fresh-water channels that joined and flowed with the Huangpu and Wusong.
translations.idiomatic: Both channels had originally opened to the sea, silted easily, and cost a fortune to dredge; they were converted into long freshwater canals linking the Huangpu and Wusong.

sentences.zh: 各於近海修閘建壩，潮汐泥沙不能壅入，內河漲，則由壩洩出歸海。

translations.literal: At each place near the sea sluice gates and dams were built so tidal mud and sand could not choke the channel; when inner rivers rose, water was released through the dams back to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Sluices and dams were built near the coast so tidal silt could not choke the canals; when inland waters rose, the excess was discharged to the sea through the dams.

sentences.zh: 复就原河逢灣取直​​，節省工費三萬餘兩，用濬附近劉河之七浦河，及附近白茆之徐六涇、東西護塘諸河。

translations.literal: He also straightened the original river where it bent, saving more than 30,000 taels in construction costs, and used the savings to dredge the Qipu River near the Liu River, and the Xu Liujing and east and west Hutang rivers near Baomao.
translations.idiomatic: Where the old channel curved, he cut a straighter course, saving over 30,000 taels, which he used to dredge the Qipu River near the Liu River and the Xu Liujing and east and west Hutang channels near Baomao.

sentences.zh: 又濬丹徒、丹陽運河，寶帶橋泖淀諸工，以次興舉，為吳中數十年之利。

translations.literal: He also dredged the Dantu and Danyang canals, the Baodai Bridge and lakes and marshes, and other works in sequence, bringing decades of benefit to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He also dredged the Dantu and Danyang canals and works at Baodai Bridge and the lake district, undertaking them in turn to the lasting benefit of the Suzhou region.

sentences.zh: 兩署兩江總督。

translations.literal: He twice served as acting governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: He twice acted as governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 十七年，擢湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1837 he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 荊、襄歲罹水災，大修堤工，其患遂弭。

translations.literal: Jing and Xiang suffered floods year after year; he undertook major dike works and the calamity was then ended.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing and Xiang basins had suffered annual flooding; after major dike repairs the threat subsided.

sentences.zh: 整頓鹽課，以減價敵私無成效，專嚴緝私之禁，銷數大增。

translations.literal: He reorganized the salt tax; reducing price to compete with smugglers had no effect, so he focused on strictly prohibiting smuggling, and sales increased greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He reformed the salt monopoly: cutting prices to undercut smugglers failed, but strict enforcement against smuggling greatly increased legal sales.

sentences.zh: 湖南鎮筸兵悍，數肇釁，巡閱撫馭，密薦總兵楊芳，擢為提督，移駐辰州，慎固苗疆屯防。

translations.literal: The troops at Zhenqian in Hunan were fierce and repeatedly provoked trouble; he toured and pacified them, secretly recommended Brigadier Yang Fang, promoted him to provincial commander, moved his headquarters to Chenzhou, and carefully secured Miao frontier garrison farms.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan's Zhenqian garrison troops were unruly and often caused incidents; Lin toured the region, recommended Brigadier Yang Fang for promotion to provincial commander, posted him at Chenzhou, and tightened defenses along the Miao frontier.

sentences.zh: 十八年，鴻臚寺卿黃爵滋請禁鴉片煙，下中外大臣議。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Honglu Temple Director Huang Juezi requested a ban on opium, and the matter was referred for discussion among Chinese and foreign ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838 Huang Juezi of the Honglu Temple petitioned to ban opium, and the court ordered discussion among all high officials.

sentences.zh: 則徐請用重典，言：「此禍不除，十年之後，不惟無可籌之餉，且無可用之兵。

translations.literal: Zexu requested severe penalties and said: "If this scourge is not removed, within ten years there will be not only no revenue that can be raised but also no troops that can be used.
translations.idiomatic: Lin urged harsh measures, writing: "Unless this evil is eradicated, within ten years the state will lack both revenue and usable troops."

sentences.zh: 」宣宗深韙之，命入覲，召對十九次。

translations.literal: " The Xuanzong Emperor deeply approved and ordered him to come to audience; he was summoned for audience nineteen times.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Daoguang strongly agreed, summoned him to court, and conferred with him nineteen times.

sentences.zh: 授欽差大臣，赴廣東查辦，十九年春，至。

translations.literal: He was appointed Imperial Commissioner and sent to Guangdong to investigate; in the spring of the nineteenth year he arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Imperial Commissioner for Guangdong and arrived there in the spring of 1839.

sentences.zh: 總督鄧廷楨已嚴申禁令，捕拏煙犯，洋商查頓先避回國。

translations.literal: Governor-General Deng Tingzhen had already strictly proclaimed the ban, arrested opium offenders, and the foreign merchant Dent had fled home first.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Deng Tingzhen had already enforced the ban and arrested offenders; the merchant Dent had fled home ahead of the crackdown.

sentences.zh: 則徐知水師提督關天培忠勇可用，令整兵嚴備。

translations.literal: Zexu knew that naval commander Guan Tianpei was loyal and brave and could be used, and ordered him to drill troops and make strict preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Naval Commander Guan Tianpei to be loyal and capable, Lin ordered him to drill the troops and prepare defenses.

sentences.zh: 檄諭英國領事義律查繳煙土，驅逐躉船，呈出煙土二萬餘箱，親蒞虎門驗收，焚於海濱，四十餘日始盡。

translations.literal: He issued a proclamation to British consul Elliot to investigate and surrender opium, expel receiving ships, and when more than 20,000 chests were produced he personally went to Humen to verify receipt and burned them on the seashore; it took more than forty days to finish.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered British Consul Charles Elliott to surrender opium and expel receiving ships; when over 20,000 chests were produced, Lin personally supervised verification at Humen and burned them on the shore over more than forty days.

sentences.zh: 請定洋商夾帶鴉片罪名，依化外有犯之例，人即正法，貨物入官，責具甘結。

translations.literal: He requested fixing the crime of foreign merchants carrying opium, following the precedent for offenders beyond the pale: the person was immediately executed according to law, goods confiscated to the state, and a written bond required.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that merchants smuggling opium be punished under the law for foreigners who commit capital crimes on Chinese soil—execution, confiscation, and a sworn bond of good conduct.

sentences.zh: 他國皆聽命，獨義律枝梧未從。

translations.literal: Other countries all obeyed; only Elliot resisted and did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Other nations complied; only Elliott refused.

sentences.zh: 於是閱視沿海砲台，以虎門為第一門戶，橫檔山、武山為第二門戶，大小虎山為第三門戶。

translations.literal: He then inspected coastal batteries: Humen as the first gateway, Hengdang Mountain and Wushan as the second gateway, and Great and Little Tiger Mountains as the third gateway.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected coastal defenses, ranking Humen as the first line, Hengdang and Wushan as the second, and the Great and Little Tiger Islands as the third.

sentences.zh: 海道至橫檔分為二支，右多暗沙，左經武山前，水深，洋船由之出入。

translations.literal: The sea route to Hengdang divided into two branches; the right had many hidden shoals, the left passed before Wushan where the water was deep, and foreign ships entered and left by it.
translations.idiomatic: At Hengdang the channel split: the right branch was shoal-ridden, the left, deeper, passed Wushan and was the route foreign vessels used.

sentences.zh: 關天培創議於此設木排鐵練二重，又增築虎門之河角砲台，英國商船後至者不敢入。

translations.literal: Guan Tianpei proposed setting up double rows of wooden stakes and iron chains here, and also building additional batteries at the river corner of Humen; later-arriving British merchant ships did not dare enter.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Tianpei proposed double lines of wooden stakes and iron chains there and new batteries at Humen's river bend; later British merchantmen dared not enter.

sentences.zh: 義律請令赴澳門載貨，冀囤煙私販，嚴斥拒之，潛泊尖沙嘴外洋。

translations.literal: Elliot requested permission to go to Macao to load cargo, hoping to hoard opium for secret sale; he was sternly refused and rebuffed, and secretly anchored off Chuanbi outside the estuary.
translations.idiomatic: Elliott asked to load cargo at Macao, intending to hoard opium for illicit trade; Lin refused and forced him to anchor secretly off Chuanbi.

sentences.zh: 會有英人毆斃華民，抗不交犯，遂斷其食物，撤買辦、工人以困之。

translations.literal: It happened that a Briton beat a Chinese man to death and resisted handing over the culprit; food supplies were then cut off and compradors and laborers withdrawn to pressure them.
translations.idiomatic: When a Briton beat a Chinese man to death and refused to surrender the killer, Lin cut off supplies and withdrew compradors and workers to pressure them.

sentences.zh: 七月，義律藉索食為名，以貨船載兵犯九龍山砲台，參將賴恩爵擊走之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Elliot used seeking food as a pretext and sent cargo ships carrying troops to attack the Kowloon batteries; Assistant Commander Lai Enjue drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In July Elliott, claiming to need provisions, sent armed cargo ships against the Kowloon batteries; Assistant Commander Lai Enjue repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 疏聞，帝喜悅，報曰：「既有此舉，不可再示柔弱。

translations.literal: When the memorial was reported, the emperor was pleased and replied: "Since this action has been taken, weakness must not be shown again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read Lin's report with pleasure and replied: "Now that you have acted, you must not show weakness again."

sentences.zh: 不患卿等孟浪，但戒卿等畏葸。

translations.literal: I do not worry that you are rash, but only warn you against timidity.
translations.idiomatic: I am not concerned that you may be rash, only that you may be timid."

sentences.zh: 」御史步際桐言出結徒虛文，則徐以彼國重然諾，不肯出結，愈不能不向索取，持之益堅。

translations.literal: " Censor Bu Jitong said that requiring bonds was empty form; Zexu argued that that country values promises, and since they would not give bonds, one could all the less fail to demand them, and held firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Bu Jitong called the bond requirement mere formality; Lin replied that Britain prized honor and, having refused the bond, must be pressed all the harder.

sentences.zh: 尋義律浼澳門洋酋轉圜，原令載煙之船回國，貨船聽官查驗。

translations.literal: Soon Elliot asked the Macao foreign chiefs to mediate; he originally ordered ships that had carried opium to return home, and cargo ships were to be inspected by officials.
translations.idiomatic: Elliott soon asked Macao's foreign community to mediate, agreeing that opium ships would leave and cargo vessels submit to inspection.

sentences.zh: 九月，商船已具結進口，義律遣兵船阻之，開砲來攻，關天培率游擊麥廷章奮擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month merchant ships had already given bonds and entered port; Elliot sent warships to block them, opened fire to attack, and Guan Tianpei led Acting Commander Mai Tingzhang to fight fiercely and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: In September merchant ships that had signed bonds tried to enter port; Elliott sent warships to block them and opened fire; Guan Tianpei and Acting Commander Mai Tingzhang drove them off.

sentences.zh: 十月，又犯虎門官湧，官軍分五路進攻，六戰皆捷。

translations.literal: In the tenth month they again attacked Guanyong at Humen; government troops advanced in five columns and won six battles in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In October the British attacked Guanyong near Humen; Qing forces advanced in five columns and won six successive engagements.

sentences.zh: 詔停止貿易，宣示罪狀，飭福建、浙江、江蘇嚴防海口。

translations.literal: An edict halted trade, proclaimed their crimes, and ordered Fujian, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu to guard the sea mouths strictly.
translations.idiomatic: The court halted trade with Britain, published their offenses, and ordered Fujian, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu to guard their coasts.

sentences.zh: 先已授則徐兩江總督，至是調補兩廣。

translations.literal: Zexu had already been appointed governor-general of the Two Jiangs; now he was transferred to fill the Two Guang posts.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had already been named governor-general of the Two Jiangs; he was now transferred to the Two Guang.

sentences.zh: 府尹曾望顏請罷各國通商，禁漁船出洋。

translations.literal: Prefect Zeng Wangyan requested ending trade with all countries and banning fishing boats from going to sea.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zeng Wangyan proposed ending trade with all nations and banning fishing boats from leaving port.

sentences.zh: 則徐疏言：「自斷英國貿易，他國喜，此盈彼絀，正可以夷制夷。

translations.literal: Zexu stated in a memorial: "Since trade with Britain was cut off, other countries are pleased; where one gains, another loses—this is exactly using barbarians to control barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Lin objected in a memorial: "Cutting off British trade pleases other nations; their gain is Britain's loss—precisely the strategy of setting foreigners against one another."

sentences.zh: 如概與之絕，轉恐聯爲一氣。

translations.literal: If trade were cut off entirely with all, one fears instead they would unite as one breath.
translations.idiomatic: If all trade were cut off, they might unite against us.

sentences.zh: 粵民以海為生，概禁出洋，其勢不可終日。

translations.literal: Cantonese live by the sea; to ban all from going to sea could not last a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese depend on the sea for their livelihood; a total ban on going to sea could not be sustained for even a day."

sentences.zh: 」時英船寄椗外洋，以利誘奸民接濟銷菸。

translations.literal: " At that time British ships lay at anchor offshore and used profit to entice traitors to supply and sell opium.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile British ships lay offshore, bribing locals to supply them with opium.

sentences.zh: 二十年春，令關天培密裝砲械，僱漁船疍戶出洋設伏，候夜順風縱火，焚毀附夷匪船，接濟始斷。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year he ordered Guan Tianpei secretly to load cannon and arms, hire fishing boats and Tanka boat people to go to sea and set ambushes, wait for night and favorable wind to set fire, burn ships attached to the foreign bandits, and supply was then cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1840 Lin had Guan Tianpei arm fishing boats and Tanka crews for night raids under favorable wind, burning supply vessels and breaking the smuggling chain.

sentences.zh: 五月，再焚夷船於磨刀洋。

translations.literal: In the fifth month foreign ships were again burned at Modaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In May more British ships were burned at Modaoyang.

sentences.zh: 諜知新來敵船揚帆北鄉，疏請沿海各省戒嚴。

translations.literal: Spies reported that newly arrived enemy ships were sailing north; he memorialized requesting all coastal provinces to be on alert.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence showed new enemy ships sailing north; Lin urged all coastal provinces to go on alert.

sentences.zh: 又言夷情詭譎，若迳赴天津求通貿易，請優示懷柔，依嘉慶年間成例，將遞詞人由內地送粵。

translations.literal: He also said foreign conduct was treacherous; if they went straight to Tianjin seeking trade, he asked that gentle treatment be shown preferentially and, following the precedent of the Jiaqing years, petitioners be sent overland to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He warned that if the British sailed to Tianjin to petition for trade, they should be treated leniently per Jiaqing precedent and escorted overland to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 六月，英船至廈門，為閩浙總督鄧廷楨所拒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month British ships reached Xiamen and were rejected by Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General Deng Tingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: In June British ships reached Xiamen and were repulsed by Governor-General Deng Tingzhen.

sentences.zh: 其犯浙者陷定海，掠寧波。

translations.literal: Those that invaded Zhejiang took Dinghai and plundered Ningbo.
translations.idiomatic: Those that struck Zhejiang captured Dinghai and raided Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 則徐上疏自請治罪，密陳兵事不可中止，略曰：「英夷所憾在粵而滋擾於浙，雖變動出於意外，其窮蹙實在意中。

translations.literal: Zexu memorialized asking to be punished and secretly stated that military affairs could not be stopped, saying in summary: "What the English barbarians resent is in Guangdong but they spread trouble in Zhejiang; though the change came unexpectedly, their distress was truly within expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Lin submitted a confession and argued privately that the war must continue: "The British resent Guangdong but now harass Zhejiang; though unexpected, their desperation was foreseeable."

sentences.zh: 惟其虛憍性成，愈窮蹙時，愈欲顯其桀驁，試其恫喝，甚且別生秘計，冀售其奸；

translations.literal: Only their arrogant nature is ingrained; the more distressed they are, the more they wish to display defiance, test intimidation, and even devise secret schemes hoping to sell their treachery;
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant by nature, the more cornered they grow, the more they bluster, threaten, and plot;

sentences.zh: 一切不得行，仍必帖耳俯伏。

translations.literal: when none of this succeeds they must still submit with bowed ears.
translations.idiomatic: but when none of this works they will submit in the end.

sentences.zh: 第恐議者以為內地船砲非外夷之敵，與其曠日持久，不如設法羈縻。

translations.literal: I only fear that deliberators will think inland ships and cannon cannot match the foreign barbarians and that rather than prolonging day after day, it is better to find means of restraint.
translations.idiomatic: I fear others will say our ships and guns cannot match theirs and prefer appeasement to a long war.

sentences.zh: 抑知夷情無厭，得步進步，威不能克，患無已時。

translations.literal: Yet know that foreign sentiment is insatiable; they advance step by step; if might cannot overcome them, calamity will have no end.
translations.idiomatic: But foreigners are never satisfied; concede once and they demand more; if force fails, trouble never ends.

sentences.zh: 他國紛紛效尤，不可不慮。

translations.literal: Other countries will follow in succession—this cannot but be considered.
translations.idiomatic: Other powers will follow suit—this must be considered."

sentences.zh: 」因請戴罪赴浙，隨營自效。

translations.literal: " He therefore asked to go to Zhejiang bearing guilt and serve with the army at his own effort.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to go to Zhejiang under punishment and serve with the troops.

sentences.zh: 七月，義律至天津，投書總督琦善，言廣東燒煙之釁，起自則徐及鄧廷楨二人，索價不與，又遭詬逐，故越境呈訴。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Elliot reached Tianjin and sent a letter to Governor Qishan, saying the quarrel over burning opium in Guangdong arose from Zexu and Deng Tingzhen; compensation was refused and they were reviled and driven off, so he crossed the border to present his complaint.
translations.idiomatic: In July Elliott reached Tianjin and wrote Governor Qishan blaming Lin and Deng for the opium burning, unpaid compensation, and insults that drove him to petition at the capital.

sentences.zh: 琦善據以上聞，上意始動。

translations.literal: Qishan reported this upward; the emperor's mind began to waver.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan reported this to the throne, and the emperor's resolve began to falter.

sentences.zh: 時英船在粵窺伺，复連敗之蓮花峰下及龍穴洲。

translations.literal: At that time British ships in Guangdong watched for openings; they were again defeated in succession below Lianhua Peak and at Longxuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile British ships off Guangdong were again defeated below Lianhua Peak and at Longxuezhou.

sentences.zh: 捷書未上，九月，詔曰：「鴉片流毒內地，特遣林則徐會同鄧廷楨查辦，原期肅清內地，斷絕來源，隨地隨時，妥為辦理。

translations.literal: Before the victory reports arrived, in the ninth month an edict said: "Opium has flowed poison into the interior; Lin Zexu was specially sent together with Deng Tingzhen to investigate, originally expecting to clear the interior and cut off the source, handling matters properly wherever and whenever.
translations.idiomatic: Before victory dispatches arrived, a September edict declared that opium poisoned the empire and Lin Zexu and Deng Tingzhen had been sent to eradicate it and cut off the source.

sentences.zh: 乃自查辦以來，內而奸民犯法不能淨盡，外而興販來源並未斷絕，沿海各省紛紛徵調，糜餉勞師，皆林則徐等辦理不善之所致。

translations.literal: Yet since the investigation began, within, law-breaking traitors could not be entirely eliminated, and without, the source of trafficking was not cut off; coastal provinces were called up one after another, wasting funds and tiring troops—all caused by Lin Zexu and others' poor handling.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since their mission began, smuggling within had not ended, supplies from abroad had not ceased, and coastal provinces were mobilized at great cost—all due to Lin Zexu's mismanagement.

sentences.zh: 」下則徐等嚴議，飭即來京，以琦善代之。

translations.literal: " Zexu and others were severely censured and ordered to come immediately to the capital; Qishan replaced them.
translations.idiomatic: Lin and Deng were censured, ordered to Beijing, and replaced by Qishan.

sentences.zh: 尋議革職，命仍回廣東備查問差委。

translations.literal: Soon it was decided to dismiss them from office; he was ordered still to return to Guangdong pending inquiry and assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon both were dismissed; Lin was ordered back to Guangdong pending further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 琦善至，義律要求賠償煙價，廈門、福州開埠通商，上怒，復命備戰。

translations.literal: When Qishan arrived, Elliot demanded compensation for the opium and opening Xiamen and Fuzhou to trade; the emperor was angry and again ordered preparations for war.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan arrived; Elliott demanded opium compensation and opening Xiamen and Fuzhou; the emperor, enraged, ordered war preparations renewed.

sentences.zh: 二十一年春，予則徐四品卿銜，赴浙江鎮海協防。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-first year Zexu was given the fourth-rank courtier title and sent to Zhejiang Zhenhai to assist in defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1841 Lin was given fourth-rank courtier status and sent to defend Zhenhai in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 時琦善雖以擅與香港逮治，和戰仍無定局。

translations.literal: At that time though Qishan had been arrested for unauthorized cession of Hong Kong, peace or war still had no fixed outcome.
translations.idiomatic: Though Qishan had been arrested for ceding Hong Kong without authorization, peace and war remained undecided.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔斥則徐在粵不能德威並用，褫卿銜，遣戍伊犁。

translations.literal: In the fifth month an edict rebuked Zexu for failing to combine virtue and awe in Guangdong, stripped his courtier title, and banished him to Yili.
translations.idiomatic: In May an edict blamed Lin for failing to balance firmness and conciliation in Guangdong, stripped his courtier rank, and exiled him to Yili.

sentences.zh: 會河決開封，中途奉命襄辦塞決，二十二年，工竣，仍赴戍，而浙江、江南師屢敗。

translations.literal: It happened that the Yellow River burst its banks at Kaifeng; on the way he was ordered to assist in blocking the breach; in the twenty-second year the work was finished and he still went to banishment, while Zhejiang and Jiangnan armies were repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River breached at Kaifeng; Lin was ordered en route to help stem it; in 1842, work done, he continued to exile while armies in Zhejiang and Jiangnan suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，和議遂成。

translations.literal: That autumn peace was concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Peace was concluded that autumn.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，新疆興治屯田，將軍布彥泰請以則徐綜其事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year colonization fields were promoted in Xinjiang; General Buyantai requested that Zexu oversee the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In 1844 Xinjiang colonization was expanded; General Buyantai asked that Lin oversee it.

sentences.zh: 週曆南八城，濬水源，闢溝渠，墾田三萬七千餘頃，請給回民耕種，改屯兵為操防，如議行。

translations.literal: He toured the eight southern cities in turn, opened water sources, dug canals and ditches, reclaimed more than 37,000 qing of fields, requested that they be given to Hui people to cultivate, and changed garrison soldiers to drill defense; as proposed, it was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He toured the eight southern cities, opened water sources, dug canals, reclaimed over 37,000 qing, assigned land to Hui farmers, and converted garrison troops to defense duties as planned.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，召還，以四五品京堂候補。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was recalled and placed on the waiting list for fourth- and fifth-rank capital posts.
translations.idiomatic: In 1845 he was recalled and placed on the waiting list for capital posts of the fourth and fifth ranks.

sentences.zh: 尋署陝甘總督。

translations.literal: Soon he served as acting governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He soon acted as governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授陝西巡撫，留甘肅，偕布彥泰治叛番，擒其酋。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Shaanxi governor but remained in Gansu, and together with Buyantai pacified rebellious tribes and captured their chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1846 he was appointed Shaanxi governor but stayed in Gansu, joining Buyantai to suppress rebellious tribes and capture their leader.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，授雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was appointed governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1847 he was appointed governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 雲南漢、回互鬥焚殺，歷十數年。

translations.literal: In Yunnan Han and Hui had fought and burned each other for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: In Yunnan, Han and Hui communities had fought and burned one another for more than a decade.

sentences.zh: 會保山回民控於京，漢民奪犯，毀官署，拆瀾滄江橋以拒，鎮道不能制。

translations.literal: It happened that Baoshan Hui petitioned at the capital; Han people seized the prisoners, destroyed government offices, and tore down the Lancang River bridge to resist; the commander and circuit intendant could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Baoshan Hui had appealed to Beijing; Han residents seized prisoners, wrecked government offices, and destroyed the Lancang River bridge to block the troops, and local commanders could not restore order.

sentences.zh: 則徐主止分良莠，不分漢、回。

translations.literal: Zexu held that one should distinguish good from bad only, not Han from Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Lin insisted on judging people by conduct, not by whether they were Han or Hui.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，親督師往剿，途中聞彌渡客回滋亂，移兵破其巢，殲匪數百。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he personally led troops to suppress them; on the way he heard that guest Hui at Midu were causing trouble and moved troops to break their nest, killing several hundred bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1848 he led the campaign in person; en route he learned of unrest among guest Hui at Midu, diverted his forces to destroy their stronghold, and killed several hundred rebels.

sentences.zh: 保山民聞風股栗，縛犯迎師，誅其首要，散其脅從，召漢、回父老諭以恩信。

translations.literal: Baoshan people trembled at the news, bound the culprits and welcomed the army, executed the ringleaders, dispersed the coerced followers, and summoned Han and Hui elders to instruct them in grace and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Baoshan residents, terrified, bound the guilty and welcomed his army; Lin executed the leaders, released the coerced, and summoned Han and Hui elders to pledge goodwill.

sentences.zh: 遂搜捕永昌、順寧、雲州、姚州歷年戕官諸重犯，威德震洽，邊境乃安。

translations.literal: He then searched out and arrested major criminals over the years who had killed officials in Yongchang, Shunning, Yunzhou, and Yaozhou; prestige and virtue spread in harmony and the border was then secure.
translations.idiomatic: He then hunted down notorious murderers of officials in Yongchang, Shunning, Yunzhou, and Yaozhou; his authority restored order along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 加太子太保，賜花翎。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，騰越邊外野夷滋擾，遣兵平之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year wild tribes beyond Tengyue border caused trouble; he sent troops and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1849 tribes beyond the Tengyue frontier raided; he sent troops and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 以病乞歸。

translations.literal: He requested retirement on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 逾年，文宗嗣位，疊詔宣召，未至，以廣西逆首洪秀全稔亂，授欽差大臣，督師進剿，並署廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: A year later the Wenzong Emperor succeeded; edicts summoning him were issued repeatedly; before he arrived, because the Guangxi rebel leader Hong Xiuquan had long been in rebellion, he was appointed Imperial Commissioner to lead troops in suppression and also acted as Guangxi governor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Emperor Xianfeng succeeded and repeatedly summoned him; before he could arrive, with Hong Xiuquan ravaging Guangxi, Lin was named Imperial Commissioner to suppress the rebellion and acting Guangxi governor.

sentences.zh: 行次潮州，病卒。

translations.literal: En route at Chaozhou he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness at Chaozhou on the march.

sentences.zh: 則徐威惠久著南服，賊聞其出，皆震悚，中道遽歿，天下惜之。

translations.literal: Zexu's prestige and kindness had long been established in the south; when rebels heard he was coming they were all shaken with fear; he died suddenly on the way and the empire mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's renown in the south had long intimidated rebels; his sudden death en route was mourned throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 遺疏上，優詔賜卹，贈太子太傅，諡文忠。

translations.literal: His final memorial was submitted; a gracious edict granted condolence payments, posthumously advanced him to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and gave the posthumous title Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His death memorial reached the throne; the emperor granted condolences, posthumously named him Grand Tutor, and gave him the posthumous title Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 雲南、江蘇並祀名宦，陝西請建專祠。

translations.literal: Yunnan and Jiangsu both enshrined him among notable officials; Shaanxi requested a dedicated temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan and Jiangsu enshrined him among notable officials; Shaanxi petitioned for a dedicated temple.

sentences.zh: 則徐才識過人，而待下虛衷，人樂為用，所蒞治績皆卓越。

translations.literal: Zexu's talent and insight surpassed others, yet he treated subordinates with open mind and people were glad to serve him; every place he governed achieved outstanding results.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's ability exceeded most men's, yet he treated subordinates with humility and won their loyalty; everywhere he served he left distinguished records.

sentences.zh: 道光之季，東南困於漕運，宣宗密詢利弊，疏陳補救本原諸策，上畿輔水利議，文宗欲命籌辦而未果。

translations.literal: At the end of Daoguang the southeast was distressed by grain transport; the Xuanzong Emperor secretly inquired into advantages and disadvantages; he memorialized policies to remedy root causes, submitted a plan on water conservancy in the capital region; the Wenzong Emperor wished to order him to undertake it but it was not realized.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Daoguang's reign the southeast struggled with grain transport; Emperor Daoguang privately consulted him; Lin proposed fundamental reforms and a capital-region waterworks plan that Emperor Xianfeng wished to implement but never did.

sentences.zh: 海疆事起，時以英吉利最強為憂，則徐獨曰：「為中國患者，其俄羅斯乎！

translations.literal: When maritime affairs arose, at the time England was considered strongest and a cause for worry; Zexu alone said: "For China the danger is perhaps Russia!
translations.idiomatic: When the coastal crisis began, Britain was feared as the strongest power; Lin alone said, "China's true danger may be Russia!"

sentences.zh: 」後其言果驗。

translations.literal: " Later his words were indeed verified.
translations.idiomatic: His prediction later proved true.

sentences.zh: 鄧廷楨 鄧廷楨，字嶰筠，江蘇江寧人。

translations.literal: Deng Tingzhen. Deng Tingzhen, style name Xiejun, was a native of Jiangning in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Tingzhen. Deng Tingzhen, style name Xiejun, was from Jiangning in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1801 he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy, and became a compiler.

sentences.zh: 屢分校鄉、會試，稱得士。

translations.literal: He repeatedly served as grader in provincial and metropolitan examinations and was praised for selecting good scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly graded provincial and metropolitan examinations and was praised for recognizing talent.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授台灣遺缺知府，浙江巡撫蔣攸銛請留浙，補寧波。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed acting prefect of Taiwan with a vacancy, but Zhejiang Governor Jiang Youqian requested he remain in Zhejiang and he was appointed to Ningbo.
translations.idiomatic: In 1810 he was named acting Taiwan prefect, but Zhejiang Governor Jiang Youqian kept him in the province and he was posted to Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，服闋，補陝西延安府，歷榆林、西安，以善折獄稱。

translations.literal: He returned on mourning for his mother; after mourning ended he was appointed to Yan'an Prefecture in Shaanxi, served successively at Yulin and Xi'an, and was known for skill in settling cases.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he was appointed Yan'an prefect in Shaanxi, served at Yulin and Xi'an, and won fame for adjudication.

sentences.zh: 平反韓城、南鄭冤獄，又全同州嫠婦母子，陝民歌頌，傳播京師。

translations.literal: He reversed wrongful convictions in Hancheng and Nanzheng, and also preserved a widow and her son in Tongzhou; Shaanxi people sang his praise and it spread to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He reversed wrongful convictions in Hancheng and Nanzheng and saved a widow and son in Tongzhou; Shaanxi sang his praises and word reached Beijing.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，超擢湖北按察使，權布政使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted over the regular course to Hubei provincial judicial commissioner and acted as provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1820 he was promoted out of turn to Hubei judicial commissioner and acted as provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 沿江民田歷年沈沒，而賦額仍在，為民累，悉請免之。

translations.literal: Along the river civilian fields had been submerged year after year while tax quotas remained, burdening the people; he requested exemption for all.
translations.idiomatic: Riverbank farmland had long been flooded while taxes remained due; he secured full remissions.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，遷江西布政使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was transferred to Jiangxi provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821 he became Jiangxi provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 以前在西安失察渭南令故出縣民柳全璧殺人罪，罣誤，奪職。

translations.literal: Because while in Xi'an he had failed to detect that Weinan magistrate had released county man Liu Quanbi who committed murder, he was implicated in error and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for failing while in Xi'an to detect that a Weinan magistrate had wrongly released a murderer, Liu Quanbi.

sentences.zh: 議戍軍台，宣宗知其無私，特免遣戍，予七品銜，發直隸委用。

translations.literal: It was decided he should serve at a military post; the Xuanzong Emperor knew he was without private motive, specially exempted banishment, gave him seventh-rank status, and sent him for employment in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Sentenced to frontier service, he was spared because the emperor knew he was blameless, given seventh-rank status, and assigned to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 尋授通永道。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed intendant of Tongzhou-Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became intendant of Tongzhou-Yongping.

sentences.zh: 四年，擢陝西按察使，遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Shaanxi provincial judicial commissioner and transferred to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1824 he became Shaanxi judicial commissioner, then provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 六年，擢安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Anhui governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1826 he was promoted to Anhui governor.

sentences.zh: 自嘉慶時，安徽多大獄，鳳、潁兩郡俗尤悍，常以兵定，責繳兵械，私藏尚多。

translations.literal: Since Jiaqing times Anhui had many major cases; Feng and Ying prefectures were especially fierce in custom and troops were often used to settle matters; they were ordered to surrender weapons but many were still hidden privately.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jiaqing, Anhui had seen many major cases; Feng and Ying were especially unruly and often required troops; weapon surrenders left many still hidden.

sentences.zh: 廷楨乃立限，責成保長，逾限及私造者置之法。

translations.literal: Tingzhen then set a deadline and held baojia chiefs responsible; those exceeding the limit or making weapons privately were punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Deng set deadlines, held baojia leaders accountable, and punished latecomers and illegal arms makers.

sentences.zh: 任吏皆得人，刁悍之風稍戢。

translations.literal: The officials he appointed were all capable men and the fierce and unruly temper was somewhat curbed.
translations.idiomatic: His appointees were capable and local lawlessness subsided.

sentences.zh: 舊例，潁州屬三人以上凶器傷人者，極邊煙瘴充軍，僉妻發配。

translations.literal: By old regulation, in Yingzhou jurisdiction when three or more persons wounded others with lethal weapons, they were sent to the farthest border miasma regions as soldiers and wives were also banished.
translations.idiomatic: By old rule, three or more armed assailants in Yingzhou were exiled to the frontier and their wives banished with them.

sentences.zh: 廷楨疏言：「悍俗誠宜重懲，婦女顧名節，多自殘求免，或自盡傷生，情在可矜，請停其例。

translations.literal: Tingzhen stated in a memorial: "Fierce custom truly should be heavily punished, but women care for chastity and many mutilate themselves to escape or even kill themselves and injure others—such feeling deserves pity; please stop this regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Deng memorialized that while harsh punishment was warranted, women often killed themselves to avoid dishonor and should not be banished with their husbands; he asked that the rule be abolished.

sentences.zh: 」遇水災，親乘舟勘賑。

translations.literal: " When flood came he personally boarded a boat to survey and provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: During floods he personally toured by boat to oversee relief.

sentences.zh: 修復安豐塘、芍陂水門，濬鳳陽沫河，加築堤閘。

translations.literal: He restored the Anfeng Pond and the sluice gates of the Quepi, dredged the Mo River in Fengyang, and added dikes and sluices.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Anfeng Pond and Quepi sluices, dredged Fengyang's Mo River, and strengthened dikes.

sentences.zh: 嚴緝捕，屢獲劇盜。

translations.literal: He strictly hunted bandits and repeatedly captured major robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Strict pursuit of bandits brought repeated captures of major gangs.

sentences.zh: 以獲南河掘堤首犯陳端，詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: Because he captured Chen Duan, chief culprit in breaching the Southern River dikes, an edict praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Capturing Chen Duan, who had breached the Southern River dikes, won imperial praise.

sentences.zh: 治皖十載，政尚安靜，境內大和。

translations.literal: He governed Anhui for ten years; policy favored quiet administration and within the borders there was great harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years in Anhui brought quiet government and widespread peace.

sentences.zh: 十五年，擢兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to governor-general of the Two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1835 he became governor-general of the Two Guang.

sentences.zh: 鴉片煙方盛行，漏銀出洋為大患。

translations.literal: Opium was then flourishing and the drain of silver overseas was a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Opium was rampant and silver draining abroad had become a national crisis.

sentences.zh: 十六年，英吉利商人以躉船載煙，廷楨禁止不許進口，猶泊外洋，嚴旨驅逐。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year English merchants used receiving ships to carry opium; Tingzhen forbade import but they still lay offshore; a stern edict ordered expulsion.
translations.idiomatic: In 1836 British merchants stored opium on receiving ships; Deng barred import but they anchored offshore until the court ordered expulsion.

sentences.zh: 沿海奸民勾結，禁令猝難斷絕。

translations.literal: Coastal traitors colluded and the ban could not be cut off in a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal smugglers colluded with foreigners and the trade could not be stopped overnight.

sentences.zh: 廷楨與提督關天培整備海防，迭於大嶼山口、急水洋獲蟹艇，載銀鉅萬，盡數充賞，破獲囤煙私販。

translations.literal: Tingzhen together with provincial commander Guan Tianpei prepared coastal defenses, repeatedly at Dayu Shan Pass and Jishui Yang captured crab boats carrying tens of thousands in silver, all confiscated as reward, and broke up hoarded opium for secret sale.
translations.idiomatic: Deng and Naval Commander Guan Tianpei strengthened defenses, seized smuggling boats with vast silver cargoes at Dayu Shan and Jishui Yang, and broke up opium hoards.

sentences.zh: 十八年，英船載屬番男婦五百餘人赴澳門居住，驅令回國。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year British ships carried more than five hundred dependent subjects of both sexes to live in Macao; they were driven to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838 British ships brought over five hundred dependents to Macao; Deng expelled them.

sentences.zh: 詔下禁煙議，疏言：「法行於豪貴，則小民易從；

translations.literal: When an edict was issued for discussion on banning opium, he stated in a memorial: "If law is enforced on the great and wealthy, the common people are easy to follow;
translations.idiomatic: When the opium ban was debated, he wrote: "Enforce the law on the powerful and commoners will follow;

sentences.zh: 令嚴於中土，則外貨自絀。

translations.literal: if prohibition is strict within China, foreign goods will naturally be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: if prohibition is strict inland, foreign opium will dry up."

sentences.zh: 」十九年，林則徐奉命至廣東，廷楨與之同心協力，盡獲躉船積煙，焚之，嚴私販之罪；

translations.literal: " In the nineteenth year Lin Zexu was ordered to Guangdong; Tingzhen worked with him with one heart and one effort, obtaining all opium hoarded on receiving ships and burning it, strictly punishing secret trafficking;
translations.idiomatic: In 1839 Lin Zexu arrived in Guangdong; Deng cooperated fully, seized and burned opium from receiving ships, and imposed harsh penalties on smugglers;

sentences.zh: 臨以兵威，屢戰皆捷，事詳則徐傳。

translations.literal: facing them with military might, repeated battles were all victorious—the details are in Zexu's biography.
translations.idiomatic: backed by force, they won repeated victories—detailed in Lin's biography.

sentences.zh: 奸民因失業，遍騰蜚語。

translations.literal: Traitors who lost their livelihood spread slander everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Displaced smugglers spread rumors everywhere.

sentences.zh: 廷楨疏陳，略曰：「臣緝懲鴉片，三載於茲。

translations.literal: Tingzhen stated in a memorial in summary: "Your subject has punished opium for three years now.
translations.idiomatic: Deng memorialized: "I have fought opium for three years.

sentences.zh: 豪猾之徒，刑僇逋逃，身家既失，怨讟遂興。

translations.literal: Powerful and cunning men, punished and fleeing, having lost family and property, resentment and slander then arose.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy offenders, punished and ruined, now slander us.

sentences.zh: 查檢為希旨，掩捕為貪功，偵伺為詭謀，推​​鞫為酷罰。

translations.literal: Inspection was called currying favor, arrest was called greed for merit, spying was called conspiracy, interrogation was called cruel punishment.
translations.idiomatic: They call inspections flattery, arrests ambition, surveillance conspiracy, and trials cruelty.

sentences.zh: 誣以納賄，目以營私。

translations.literal: They falsely accuse of taking bribes and label as seeking private gain.
translations.idiomatic: They accuse us of bribery and self-dealing.

sentences.zh: 譏建議為急於理財，訾新例為輕於改律，狂悖紛熒，無非為煙匪洩憤。

translations.literal: They mock proposals as haste to enrich the treasury and revile new regulations as lightly changing the law—reckless and confused, all nothing but venting anger for opium bandits.
translations.idiomatic: They mock reform as greed and new laws as rash—all to avenge opium smugglers."

sentences.zh: 」詔慰勉之。

translations.literal: " An edict comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with encouragement.

sentences.zh: 調兩江、雲貴，皆未赴，閩防方急，遂調閩浙總督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Two Jiangs and Yunnan-Guizhou but did not go; Fujian defense was urgent and he was transferred to Fujian-Zhejiang governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the Two Jiangs and Yunnan-Guizhou, he never took those posts; with Fujian under threat he became Fujian-Zhejiang governor-general.

sentences.zh: 購洋砲十四運閩，以閩洋無內港，砲台建於海灘，沙浮不固，奏改為砲墩，囊沙堆築，外護以船。

translations.literal: He purchased fourteen foreign cannon for Fujian; because Fujian seas had no inner harbors, batteries built on beaches were unstable on floating sand; he memorialized to change them to gun platforms, bagging sand in heaps and protecting them outward with boats.
translations.idiomatic: He bought fourteen foreign guns for Fujian; sandy beaches made batteries unstable, so he built sand-filled gun platforms shielded by boats.

sentences.zh: 募水勇飾商船出洋巡緝。

translations.literal: He recruited water braves and fitted merchant ships to patrol at sea.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited coastal fighters and armed merchant vessels for patrols.

sentences.zh: 二十年三月，英船窺廈門，遣提督程恩高等迎敵於梅林澳，擊走之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twentieth year British ships watched Xiamen; he sent Provincial Commander Cheng Engao and others to meet the enemy at Meilin Bay and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: In March 1840 British ships probed Xiamen; Provincial Commander Cheng Engao repulsed them at Meilin Bay.

sentences.zh: 奸民勾通出洋運煙，分責水陸師嚴緝，遇即攻擊，迭有殲擒。

translations.literal: Traitors colluded to carry opium to sea; he assigned responsibility to land and naval forces for strict pursuit, attacking whenever encountered, with repeated captures and kills.
translations.idiomatic: Smugglers still shipped opium offshore; land and naval forces attacked on sight with repeated successes.

sentences.zh: 六月，敵船駛入廈門，求通貿易，阻之，遂開砲，來撲砲台，參將陳勝元、守備陳光福奮擊，斃其前隊數人，發砲傷敵甚眾，乃遁。

translations.literal: In the sixth month enemy ships entered Xiamen seeking trade; blocked, they opened fire and came to storm the batteries; Assistant Commander Chen Shengyuan and Garrison Commander Chen Guangfu fought fiercely, killed several in the vanguard, and fired cannon wounding many enemies, and they then fled.
translations.idiomatic: In June enemy ships entered Xiamen seeking trade; when blocked they bombarded the forts; Chen Shengyuan and Chen Guangfu killed the vanguard, wounded many, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 其分犯浙洋者，陷定海，廷楨率師赴剿，行次清風嶺，詔以閩防緊要，止其赴浙，遂駐兵泉州，招募練勇。

translations.literal: Those that invaded Zhejiang seas took Dinghai; Tingzhen led troops to suppress them; at Qingfeng Ridge an edict said Fujian defense was urgent and stopped his going to Zhejiang; he then stationed troops at Quanzhou and recruited militia.
translations.idiomatic: While British forces took Dinghai in Zhejiang, Deng marched to relieve it but was ordered to remain in Fujian; he stationed troops at Quanzhou and raised militia.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「英船二十餘艘聚泊定海，內地師船恐難驟近，必改造堅大之船，多配砲火，間道而進，方能制勝。

translations.literal: He stated in a memorial: "More than twenty British ships are gathered at Dinghai; inland war junks may hardly approach suddenly; one must rebuild stout large ships with many cannon and advance by hidden routes before one can overcome.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Over twenty British ships lie at Dinghai; our junks cannot approach; we must build larger warships with heavy guns and take indirect routes to prevail."

sentences.zh: 」 九月，詔以廷楨等在粵辦理不善，轉滋事端，與林則徐同奪職。

translations.literal: " In the ninth month an edict said Tingzhen and others had handled matters poorly in Guangdong and stirred up trouble; together with Lin Zexu they were stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In September an edict blamed Deng and Lin for mishandling Guangdong and causing trouble; both were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，琦善撤沿海兵備，虎門失守，复追論廷楨久任兩廣，廢弛營務，與則徐同戍伊犁。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Qishan withdrew coastal defenses and Humen fell; they again pursued Tingzhen's long tenure in the Two Guang and lax garrison duties; together with Zexu he was banished to Yili.
translations.idiomatic: In 1841 Qishan weakened coastal defenses and Humen fell; Deng's long Guangdong tenure was blamed; he and Lin were exiled to Yili.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，釋還。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In 1843 he was released.

sentences.zh: 尋予三品頂戴，授甘肅布政使。

translations.literal: Soon he was given third-rank rank insignia and appointed Gansu provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He soon received third-rank insignia and became Gansu provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 議清查荒地，親往歷勘，由銀州東盡洮、隴，西極酒泉，得田一萬九千四百餘頃，又番貢地一千五百餘頃，寧夏馬廠地歸公一百餘頃，熟地昇科，荒者招墾，詔嘉其勤，复二品頂戴。

translations.literal: Discussing survey of wasteland, he personally went to inspect; from east of Yinchuan to Tao and Long in the west and Jiuquan at the extreme west, he found 19,400-odd qing of fields, also 1,500-odd qing of tribute lands, and more than 100 qing of Ningxia horse-pasture land returned to the state; established tax on cultivated land and recruited settlers for waste land; an edict praised his diligence and restored second-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying wasteland from Yinchuan east to Jiuquan west, he registered nearly 19,400 qing of fields, 1,500 qing of tribute land, and 100 qing of Ningxia pasture, taxing arable land and recruiting settlers; the emperor restored his second-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，擢陝西巡撫，署陝甘總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to Shaanxi governor and acted as governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1845 he became Shaanxi governor and acting Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general.

sentences.zh: 番匪擾蒙部，遣兵邀擊於硫磺溝，平之。

translations.literal: Tribal bandits harassed Mongol banners; he sent troops to intercept them at Liuhuang Gou and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal raiders harassed Mongolia; he defeated them at Liuhuang Gou.

sentences.zh: 尋回任。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to his regular post.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resumed his regular duties.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1846 he died in office.

sentences.zh: 廷楨治行早為時稱，屢躓屢起，宣宗知之深，故卒用之。

translations.literal: Tingzhen's administrative conduct had long been praised in his time; he stumbled and rose repeatedly; the Xuanzong Emperor knew him deeply and therefore used him to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Deng's reputation for governance was long established; though he fell and rose repeatedly, Emperor Daoguang trusted him to the end.

sentences.zh: 績學好士，幕府多名流，論學不輟。

translations.literal: He was learned and loved scholars; his staff had many famous men and he never ceased discussing learning.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and fond of scholars, he kept distinguished advisers and debated scholarship constantly.

sentences.zh: 尤精於音韻之學，所著筆記、詩、詞並行世。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in phonology; his notebooks, poetry, and lyrics all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in phonology; his notes, poetry, and lyrics all circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子爾恆，亦官至陝西巡撫，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Erheng also rose to Shaanxi governor and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Erheng also became Shaanxi governor and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 當廷楨之去福建也，逾年，英兵復至，陷廈門，遂窺台灣。

translations.literal: When Tingzhen left Fujian, a year later English troops came again, took Xiamen, and then watched Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: A year after Deng left Fujian, British forces returned, took Xiamen, and threatened Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 總兵達洪阿偕台灣道姚瑩屢卻之。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Da Hong'a together with Taiwan Circuit Intendant Yao Ying repeatedly repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Da Hong'a and Taiwan Intendant Yao Ying repeatedly drove them back.

sentences.zh: 及和議成，同獲譴。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded they were both punished.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was made both were censured.

sentences.zh: 達洪阿 達洪阿，字厚庵，富察氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Da Hong'a. Da Hong'a, style name Hou'an, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Da Hong'a. Da Hong'a, style name Hou'an, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 由護軍洊擢總兵。

translations.literal: From guard soldier he was promoted step by step to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the guards to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年，調台灣鎮。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he was transferred to Taiwan command.
translations.idiomatic: In 1835 he was transferred to command Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 十八年，剿嘉義縣匪沈和等，賜花翎，加提督銜。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he suppressed the bandit Shen He and others in Jiayi County, was granted the peacock feather, and given the provincial commander rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838 he suppressed bandits led by Shen He in Jiayi, received the peacock feather, and acting provincial commander rank.

sentences.zh: 二十一年八月，英兵船至雞籠海口，達洪阿與姚瑩督兵御之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-first year English warships reached Jilong harbor; Da Hong'a together with Yao Ying directed troops to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In August 1841 British warships reached Keelung; Da Hong'a and Yao Ying led the defense.

sentences.zh: 副將邱鎮功燃巨砲折其桅，敵船衝礁破碎，擒斬甚眾，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: Vice Commander Qiu Zhenggong fired a great cannon and broke their mast; the enemy ship struck a reef and was shattered; many were captured and beheaded; he was granted double-eyed peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander Qiu Zhenggong shattered a mast with heavy guns; the enemy ship wrecked on reefs; many were killed or captured; Da Hong'a received double peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 九月，敵船再至雞籠三沙灣，复卻之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month enemy ships again came to Jilong Sansha Bay and were again repulsed.
translations.idiomatic: In September the British returned to Sansha Bay near Keelung and were repulsed again.

sentences.zh: 剿平嘉義、鳳山土匪，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: He suppressed bandits in Jiayi and Fengshan and was given the hereditary rank of Cavalry Captain.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified bandits in Jiayi and Fengshan and received the hereditary rank of Cavalry Captain.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，敵船犯淡水、彰化間之大安港，欲入口。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year enemy ships violated the Da'an harbor between Tamsui and Zhanghua and wished to enter.
translations.idiomatic: In 1842 enemy ships approached Da'an harbor between Tamsui and Zhanghua intending to land.

sentences.zh: 達洪阿謀於姚瑩，瑩曰：「此未可與海上爭鋒，必以計殲之。

translations.literal: Da Hong'a consulted Yao Ying; Ying said: "This cannot be met in open combat at sea; one must use stratagem to destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: Da Hong'a consulted Yao Ying, who said they could not fight at sea and must use stratagem.

sentences.zh: 」乃募漁舟投敵任鄉導，誘令從土地公港入，擱淺中流，伏發，大破之，落水死者無算，其竄入漁舟者，擊斬殆盡。

translations.literal: " They then recruited fishing boats to offer themselves as guides to the enemy, induced them to enter by Tugonggang, where they ran aground midstream; ambush was sprung and they were greatly defeated; those who fell into the water died beyond counting; those who fled into fishing boats were nearly all killed.
translations.idiomatic: They hired fishing boats to mislead the British into Tugonggang, where the ships grounded; ambush troops annihilated them, few survivors escaping ashore.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉台灣三次破敵，達洪阿等智勇兼施，大揚國威，賜號阿克達春巴圖魯，加太子太保銜。

translations.literal: An edict praised Taiwan's three defeats of the enemy; Da Hong'a and others combined wisdom and courage and greatly raised national prestige; he was granted the title Akedachun Batulu and the rank of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised three Taiwanese victories; Da Hong'a was named Akedachun Batulu and made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 敵船遊奕外洋，乘間掩擊，迭有俘獲，遂不復至。

translations.literal: Enemy ships cruised offshore; taking advantage of intervals they were struck in surprise attacks with repeated captures, and they then did not come again.
translations.idiomatic: Patrols struck British ships offshore whenever opportunity offered, and the enemy stopped returning.

sentences.zh: 既而英師再陷定海，浙江、江蘇軍屢挫，乃議和。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the English army again took Dinghai; Zhejiang and Jiangsu armies were repeatedly defeated and peace was then discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the British retook Dinghai; defeats in Zhejiang and Jiangsu led to peace talks.

sentences.zh: 英將濮鼎查訴稱台灣所戮皆遭風難民，達洪阿等冒功捏奏，命總督怡良赴台灣查辦。

translations.literal: English General Pottinger complained that those killed in Taiwan were all shipwrecked civilians; Da Hong'a and others had falsely claimed merit; the emperor ordered Governor Yiliang to go to Taiwan to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: General Pottinger claimed the Taiwanese victims were shipwrecked civilians and accused Da Hong'a of fabricating victories; Governor Yiliang was sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 至即傳旨革職逮問，兵民不服，勢洶洶，達洪阿等撫慰乃散。

translations.literal: On arrival the edict was transmitted to dismiss and arrest them; soldiers and civilians were dissatisfied and the situation was turbulent; Da Hong'a and others pacified them and they then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The investigators arrived to arrest them; troops and civilians rioted until Da Hong'a calmed them.

sentences.zh: 至京，下刑部獄，尋釋之，予三等侍衛，充哈密辦事大臣。

translations.literal: Reaching the capital he was imprisoned in the Ministry of Justice; soon released, given third-rank bodyguard, and appointed commissioner at Hami.
translations.idiomatic: In Beijing he was jailed, then released, made a third-rank guardsman, and posted to Hami.

sentences.zh: 歷伊犁參贊大臣，西寧辦事大臣。

translations.literal: He successively served as assistant at Ili and commissioner at Xining.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as assistant at Ili and commissioner at Xining.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，偕陝甘總督布彥泰剿平黑錯寺番匪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he together with Shaanxi-Gansu Governor-General Buyantai suppressed and pacified the Heicuosi tribal bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1846 he joined Governor-General Buyantai to suppress the Heicuosi tribal rebels.

sentences.zh: 三十年，授副都統。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was appointed vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1850 he was appointed vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，從大學士賽尚阿勦賊廣西，破紫金山西南砲台。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he followed Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a to suppress rebels in Guangxi and captured the southwest batteries of Zijin Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he followed Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a against rebels in Guangxi and took the southwest batteries on Zijin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 以病回京。

translations.literal: He returned to the capital on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced his return to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 三年，粵匪犯畿輔，率八旗兵赴臨洺關進剿。

translations.literal: In the third year Guangdong rebels invaded the capital region; he led Eight Banner troops to Linming Pass to advance in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 he led Banner troops to Linming Pass when Guangdong rebels threatened the capital region.

sentences.zh: 從欽差大臣勝保擊賊靜海，四戰皆捷，追至下西河，副都統佟鑑、天津知縣謝子澄陣亡。

translations.literal: He followed Imperial Commissioner Sheng Bao to attack rebels at Jinghai; four battles were all victorious; pursuit reached Xiaxihe; Vice Commander-in-Chief Tong Jian and Tianjin magistrate Xie Zicheng died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Imperial Commissioner Sheng Bao at Jinghai, he won four battles and pursued the enemy to Xiaxihe, where Vice Commander Tong Jian and Tianjin Magistrate Xie Zicheng fell.

sentences.zh: 詔斥達洪阿先退，革職，留營效力。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked Da Hong'a for retreating first, dismissed him from office, and kept him at camp to render service.
translations.idiomatic: An edict blamed Da Hong'a for retreating first, stripped his rank, but kept him at camp.

sentences.zh: 四年，敗賊獻縣，復原官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he defeated rebels at Xian County and was restored to his original office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 he defeated rebels at Xian County and was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 尋追賊阜城，受傷，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Soon pursuing rebels at Fucheng he was wounded and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, wounded while pursuing rebels at Fucheng, he died in camp.

sentences.zh: 贈都統銜，予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職，諡壯武。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the rank of commander-in-chief, granted the hereditary ranks of Cavalry Captain plus one Cloud Cavalry Captain, and given the posthumous title Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously named commander-in-chief, granted hereditary Cavalry Captain and Cloud Cavalry Captain ranks, and given the posthumous title Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 姚瑩自有傳。

translations.literal: Yao Ying has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Ying has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 論曰：林則徐才略冠時，禁煙一役，承宣宗嚴切之旨，操之過急；

translations.literal: The comment says: Lin Zexu's talent and strategy topped his age; in the opium prohibition campaign he carried out the Xuanzong Emperor's stern and urgent intent and handled matters too hastily;
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Lin Zexu's ability was unmatched in his day; in suppressing opium he carried out Emperor Daoguang's stern orders too hastily;

sentences.zh: 及敵氛蹈瑕他犯，遂遭讒屏斥。

translations.literal: when the enemy took advantage of flaws and invaded elsewhere, he then suffered slander and dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: when the enemy exploited openings and struck elsewhere, slander drove him from office.

sentences.zh: 論者謂粵事始終倚之，加之操縱，潰裂當不致此。

translations.literal: Commentators say that if Guangdong affairs had been entrusted to him throughout and he had been given control, the collapse would not have reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that had Guangdong policy rested in his hands throughout, the disaster would not have been so severe.

sentences.zh: 則徐瀕謫，疏陳：「自道光元年以來，粵關徵銀三千餘萬兩，收其利必防其害。

translations.literal: On the verge of dismissal Zexu stated in a memorial: "Since the first year of Daoguang, Guangdong customs have collected more than 30 million taels of silver; in receiving its profit one must guard against its harm.
translations.idiomatic: Facing dismissal, Lin wrote: "Since 1821 Guangdong customs have collected over thirty million taels; profits must be weighed against dangers.

sentences.zh: 使以關稅十分之一制砲造船，制夷已可裕如。

translations.literal: If one used one-tenth of customs revenue to build cannon and ships, controlling the barbarians would already be ample.
translations.idiomatic: Spending a tenth of customs revenue on guns and ships would have sufficed to control the foreigners."

sentences.zh: 」誠為讜論。

translations.literal: " This was truly sound counsel.
translations.idiomatic: That was sound counsel.

sentences.zh: 惟當時內治廢弛，外情隔膜，言和言戰，皆昧機宜，其禍豈能倖免哉？

translations.literal: Only at that time internal governance was lax, foreign conditions were cut off by a screen, and whether speaking of peace or war all were ignorant of the right moment—how could calamity be escaped by luck?
translations.idiomatic: But domestic government was decaying, foreign realities misunderstood, and advocates of peace and war alike misjudged the moment—how could disaster have been avoided?

sentences.zh: 鄧廷楨與則徐同心禦侮，克保岩疆。

translations.literal: Deng Tingzhen together with Zexu with one heart resisted insult and was able to secure the rocky frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Tingzhen stood with Lin against foreign aggression and helped secure the coast.

sentences.zh: 若達洪阿、姚瑩卻敵台灣，固由守禦有方，亦因敵非專注，朝廷皆不得已而罪之，諸人卒皆復起，而名節播宇內、煥史冊矣。

translations.literal: As for Da Hong'a and Yao Ying repelling the enemy in Taiwan, it was indeed because defense was well ordered, but also because the enemy was not focused there; the court punished them all as matters of necessity, yet these men were all eventually raised up again, and their fame and integrity spread through the realm and shine in the historical records.
translations.idiomatic: Da Hong'a and Yao Ying defended Taiwan effectively, though partly because Britain was not fully committed there; the court punished them reluctantly, yet all were eventually rehabilitated, and their reputations endure in history.
